note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Headache episodes described as hot sensation with severe headaches affecting work.
  - Associated symptoms: reduced appetite, tingling in both arms, palpitations (feeling heart racing), and intermittent shortness of breath.
  - Onset/timing: Symptoms began after changing jobs; occur randomly and mostly during work; not clearly tied to commute or exercise.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Headache: occurs at work, comes and goes.
  - Weight loss: about 5 pounds; not intentional.
  - Tingling: new symptom starting with current period.
  - Breathing: brief episodes of shortness of breath, mainly at work or while seated; not with exercise.
  - Libido: decreased; same time frame as job change.
- ENT symptoms:
  - None reported (no throat swelling, hoarseness, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor, dyspnea on exertion, or facial/lip/uvular swelling).
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - History of hyperthyroidism; on thyroxine.
  - No prior details of similar prior episodes.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: not documented.
  - Medications: thyroxine for hyperthyroidism; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social context:
  - Occupation: lawyer in London; high work stress.
  - Alcohol: couple of glasses of wine weekly.
  - Smoking: no.
  - Recreational drugs: none.
  - Accompaniment: not stated.

Objective:
- Observable findings:
  - Not recorded in transcript.
- Airway/breathing:
  - Patient reports intermittent shortness of breath; no description of stridor or significant airway distress.
- Mental status/associated features:
  - Not documented.
- Vitals/examination:
  - Not recorded.
- Other persons present:
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Primary impression:
  - Systemic symptom complex (headache, weight loss, tachycardia/palpitations, intermittent dyspnea, tingling) in a patient with known hyperthyroidism; no ENT-specific symptoms identified.
- Considerations:
  - Thyroid-related etiologies or adjustment of thyroid function; stress-related autonomic symptoms.
  - No acute ENT pathology evident from history.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Recommend in-person clinic evaluation for formal examination (cardiorespiratory assessment) and thyroid function testing.
- Patient/caregiver instructions:
  - Schedule appointment via app to see one of the clinic doctors; clinician will review history and perform examination and tests.
  - Expect thyroid function blood tests (thyroxine) and heart/breathing assessment during visit.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Not documented in transcript.
- Follow-up:
  - In-person clinic appointment to assess cardiac/respiratory status and thyroid function; further management to be determined after exam and labs.
  - Potential referrals (ENT/allergy) discussed as needed based on exam findings.
- Additional notes:
  - No acute emergency actions (e.g., adrenaline) were taken or discussed.
  - No explicit emergency contact instructions provided in transcript.
